explanation: The protonated ether is attacked by the halide at the less hindered sp³ carbon (SN2) or ionises at a 3° carbon (SN1); with excess HX both alkyl groups end as halides. An aryl–O bond survives as the phenol.
tip: Excess HBr/HI + heat: alkyl–O → alkyl–X; aryl–O stays as Ar–OH.

traps.why: The aryl–O bond never breaks: SN2 cannot happen on an sp² ring carbon. The aryl side ends up as the phenol; only the alkyl side becomes the halide.
